title: Crash on startup with Electron 40.x built with v8_enable_sandbox=false (Illegal Access in IndirectBaseHandle::IsEmpty)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 26100

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.2.6

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior


When built with the following flags:
```
  v8_enable_sandbox = false
  v8_enable_pointer_compression = false
```
The application should start normally (same behavior as with my custom 39.2.6 build with the same flags).

### Actual Behavior

Electron 40.x crashes on startup (Apparently this only happens on Windows).

`Unhandled error in main process: Error: ERR_FAILED (-2) loading 'http://localhost:8100'
    at rejectAndCleanup (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:83298)
    at finishListener (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:83460)
    at WebContents.stopLoadingListener (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:83847)
    at WebContents.emit (node:events:508:28)
    at WebContents.emit (node:domain:489:12) {
  errno: -2,
  code: 'ERR_FAILED',
  url: 'http://localhost:8100'`

Crash dump points to an Illegal Access Exception at IndirectBaseHandle::IsEmpty in v8-handle-base.h.





### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Steps to reproduce**

Clone Electron source for 40.0.0-beta.X.

Configure GN with:
```
  v8_enable_sandbox = false
  v8_enable_pointer_compression = false
```
  
Build Electron (e.g. ninja -C out/Release electron).

Run my app with the newly built Electron.

The app immediately fails to boot; main process throws the ERR_FAILED (-2) error, and the minidump shows an Illegal Access in IndirectBaseHandle::IsEmpty.

[4fcd5d3e-4d1a-4e01-b906-71bf6080c7b4.dmp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24119662/4fcd5d3e-4d1a-4e01-b906-71bf6080c7b4.dmp)

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Electron 40.x on Windows x64 crashes at startup when built with:

v8_enable_sandbox = false
v8_enable_pointer_compression = false


This configuration worked in Electron 39.2.6 but now causes an access violation in V8 (IndirectBaseHandle::IsEmpty).
Based on investigation, newer Chromium/V8 versions appear to implicitly require the V8 sandbox on Windows, even though GN still allows disabling it.

Suggestion:
If v8_enable_sandbox = false is no longer supported on Windows, it would help to:

Document this explicitly in Electron 40+ release notes, or

Add a GN/build-time or early runtime check to fail fast with a clear error instead of crashing.

This would prevent confusion for custom Electron builds relying on older V8 configurations.

comments.body:
> It would be great if this patch is kept even if Electron stops supporting 32-bit systems.
Otherwise people trying to build Electron without the v8 sandbox will encounter problems and likely open issues.

The Electron maintainers have already mentioned in many threads (e.g. ones about debug builds) that building with different flags than the ones the official builds use is unsupported and if you do so you are on your own. So technically you were already doing the wrong thing by opening an issue here for your custom build problem, you just got lucky that people decided to help you anyway this time. So I would be very surprised if they decide to keep that patch around longer than necessary, I recommend you read: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/docs/development/patches.md#patch-justification (keeping a patch around that isn't required for the official builds goes against the goal of keeping the patch count and maintenance burden to a minimum).

comments.body:
> I will try to help anyone and I will continue to pay Electron maintainers to continue to allow custom forks without the memory cage.

> As stated here https://<redacted-host>/blog/v8-memory-cage

>> Though somewhat complicated, it is also possible to build a custom version of Electron with pointer compression disabled, if you decide you want a different trade-off for your particular use case
> If the policy has changed: it's not longer possible to build a custom version of electron with the memory cage or pointer compression disabled, then I think that is a very big deal and they need to announce that more formally. And I think that would be a betrayal of their users.

The Electron maintainers obviously cannot ban custom forks. My understanding of the "policy", based on responses on other threads is that the Electron maintainers will provide support for builds that use the same set of build flags that the official builds use, for the same platforms that official builds are provided for, but if you use different build flags or target different platforms, you won't get any support/it is on you to keep your custom builds keep working.

So no I don't think the policy has ever changed, there is a massive difference between "it is possible for you to create a custom build that does x" vs "creating a custom build that does x is supported by the maintainers", you have just been lucky so far that making builds without the memory cage and pointer compression has been possible, because Chromium still provides 32-bit builds that don't support those two things. When upstream stops needing build flags to opt-out of those two things, don't be surprised if it stops working in Electron too.
